deep.reconstruction:
The page has three layers.

(A) Lecture draft (upright, ink, top). It is the opening of a lecture on complex integration: "In the last lecture we stopped while deriving some general theorems about Cauchy's integrals between imaginary limits." A sketch shows the plane with axes (labelled x and y) and a curve from a to b. With z = x + iy, f(z) = u + iv and dz = dx + i dy, multiplying out under the integral sign gives

  ∫_a^b f(z) dz = ∫ (u + iv)(dx + i dy) = ∫ (u dx − v dy) + i ∫ (v dx + u dy).

The Cauchy–Riemann equations are written down:
- ∂u/∂x = ∂v/∂y,
- ∂u/∂y = −∂v/∂x.

The text says that, after the multiplication under the integral sign, both the real part and the imaginary part are complete (exact) differentials. Spelled out [mine]:
- u dx − v dy is exact iff ∂u/∂y = ∂(−v)/∂x, i.e. u_y = −v_x.
- v dx + u dy is exact iff ∂v/∂y = ∂u/∂x.

This is what is needed for ∫_a^b f(z) dz to be independent of the path from a to b. The text then starts on the converse ("Um den umgekehrten Satz zu beweisen, dass …", "we remark that the theorem can also be stated thus …") and breaks off. This is Riemann's standard Göttingen lecture material on functions of a complex variable.

(B) Scratch work on iteration of Möbius maps (right side, pencil). It begins with f(x) = (α + x)/(b + x) and the fixed-point equations x = f(x) and x = f²(x). A circle is drawn, probably the circle on which the iterates move. The map is then replaced by f(x) = 1/(β + x), and the alternating composition is written out as

  f²(x) = α + 1/(β + 1/(α + 1/(β + x))).

This is the period-2 continued fraction [α, β, α, β, …]. Its limit is a fixed point of a Möbius transformation. For example [mine], with g(x) = α + 1/(β + x), the period-1 fixed point satisfies x² + (β − α)x − αβ − 1 = 0. This links directly to the next page, which contracts a continued fraction into its even part: a_{2m} = α_{2m} α_{2m−1}, b_{2m} = α_{2m} + α_{2m+1}.

(C) Upside-down pencil calculations (lower half). The clearest lines are

  Σ q^{2m}/(m!)² (φ(m) − φ(0)) : Σ q^{2m}/(m!)²  together with  + φ(0) − log q.

Here φ(m) is evidently the logarithmic derivative of Π(m) = Γ(m+1), i.e. ψ(m+1), so φ(m) − φ(0) = H_m (harmonic number) and φ(0) = −γ. Σ q^{2m}/(m!)² = I_0(2q) is the regular solution of t v'' + v' − v = 0 with t = q². The previous page has this equation in the form 4t ∂²v/∂(log t)² + …. The combination

  (φ(0) − log q) I_0(2q) + Σ q^{2m}/(m!)² (φ(m) − φ(0))

is exactly the logarithmic second solution, i.e. K_0(2q). So Riemann is forming the ratio K_0/I_0 = φ(0) − log q + Σ(…)/Σ(…), and the lines with "Σ/Σ = 1 + …" and (m+1)² denominators appear to manipulate the shifted series (m → m+1). This is plausibly done to expand that ratio as a continued fraction, which ties in with layer (B) and the next page.

The numerical fragments (4/(1 − 2/3), 8/5, 9, 36, 3·48/511, "3/2 = 1 − 2/3 − 4", "8/5·9 − 1 … − 9 − 8/5·3") look like test evaluations, possibly with q² = 9. They are too fragmentary to reconstruct with certainty.
errors: The formula ∫(u dx − v dy) + i∫(v dx + u dy) is correct. The machine transcription is right if the second bracket reads (v dx + u dy); if the hand actually wrote (u dx + u dy), that is a slip of the pen.
The converse theorem is announced but not carried out; the draft breaks off mid-sentence.
The upside-down identity '8/5 Σ … + 1 = Σ …/(m+1)²' cannot be verified: coefficients are mixed with numerical test values, and some terms (φ(m+1)² vs φ(m+1)) are uncertain.
'3/2 = 1 − 2/3 − 4' is false as written; it is probably a fragmentary scratch line or misread.

results.what: Integral of f(z) dz split into real and imaginary line integrals; Cauchy–Riemann equations imply both are exact differentials, hence path independence
results.modern_name: Cauchy's integral theorem (via Green / exact differentials) and Cauchy–Riemann equations

results.what: Fixed points of a Möbius map and its second iterate; periodic continued fraction α + 1/(β + 1/(α + …))
results.modern_name: Fixed points of linear fractional transformations / periodic continued fractions
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Lagrange, Galois (periodic continued fractions); Möbius

results.what: Logarithmic second solution of t v'' + v' − v = 0 in the form (φ(0) − log q) Σ q^{2m}/(m!)² + Σ q^{2m}/(m!)² (φ(m) − φ(0)), with φ the digamma function, and the ratio to the regular solution
results.modern_name: Series for the modified Bessel function K_0 (Macdonald function) / Neumann-type second solution Y_0
results.usually_credited_to: C. Neumann (1867), Hankel (1869); log-type series via the Frobenius method

deep.surprise_reason: The complex-integration lecture draft is routine and known Riemann teaching material. The upside-down scratch shows Riemann, apparently in the 1850s, working with the explicit digamma/log series of the second solution of Bessel's equation of order zero (K_0) and its ratio to I_0, probably aiming at a continued fraction. That predates Neumann's 1867 publication, but such series were obtainable by standard methods and the work is fragmentary, so it is only a modestly notable unpublished detail.

transcription_corrections: Second bracket of the first formula should read (v dx + u dy)√−1, as the machine transcription has it; the hand may look like 'u dx'.
'Schlossen wir dann unter den Integralzeichen' is more likely 'Schaffen/Führten wir dann unter dem Integralzeichen die Multiplication aus' (carrying out the multiplication under the integral sign).
'und also nöthig ist' is likely 'und also [hinreichend und] nöthig ist' or 'was also nöthig ist'; the sense is a necessary condition for path independence.
f(z) = u + v√−1 is written with an overstruck 'i' (u + v i / √−1).
Upside-down block: 'Σ q^{2m}/(m!)² (φ(m) − φ(0)) : Σ q^{2m}/(m!)²' and '+ φ(0) − log q' are the key readable lines; φ is the digamma function (log-derivative of Π).
